events.title: Employee falls from unguarded scaffold and is killed
events.description: 1 worker death. Employer: Forsythe, Inc. Washington, DC. At 10:00 a.m. on May 18, 2024, Employee #1, employed as a mason, was performing masonry work using a scaffold. The scaffold was unguarded, and the employee fell approximately 30 feet to a concrete slab. The employee sustained multiple fractures from the fall and was later pronounced dead from the injuries.

events.title: Employee with COVID-19 infection dies
events.description: 1 worker death. Employer: Capital Group Companies Inc. Washington, DC. At 9:30 a.m. on September 20, 2023, an employee was on business travel. The employee died due to complications from COVID-19.

While nearing the work area, an estimated 7-feet above ground level, the employee leaned back against the rail on the scaffold. At 2:00 p.m. on October 13, 2022, an employee was standing on a ladder when he removed a ceiling tile to replace a bulb ina light fixture. As the employee attempted to complete his task, he was electrocuted and died.

events.title: Employee is killed in fall into stairwell
events.description: 1 worker death. Employer: Intelligent Investment, Inc. Washington, DC. At 1:00 p.m. on July 28, 2022, an employee fell into a stairwell and was killed.

events.title: Employee dies of unknown causes

events.title: Employee with COVID-19 infection dies
events.description: 1 worker death. Employer: Catholic Charities Of The Archdiocese Of Washington, Inc. Washington, DC. At 3:00 a.m. on April 4, 2022, an employee who had been working at a men's shelter performing administrative duties died from COVID-19. The employee had contracted COVID-19 in January 2022 and may have died from complications related to that illness. The date, time and other details leading up to exposure are notindicated in the narrative. Information regarding engineering, administrative and personal protective equipment controls for COVID-19 are also not included in the narrative.

Employee possibly received electrical shock (277 volts) and fell approximately five feet from the ladder. The employee received ahead injury and was killed.

events.title: Employee with COVID-19 infection dies

At approximately 9:30 a.m. on January 12, 2021, an employee was performing environmental services cleaning duties in the CATH Laboratory in between procedures. The employee contracted COVID-19 and later died.

events.title: Employee with COVID-19 infection dies

events.title: Employee hoisting drywall cart is killed in fall
events.description: 1 worker death. Employer: Component Assembly Systems, Inc. Washington, DC. At 8:00 a.m. on September 28, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a drywall company, was working at a multi-employer construction project, a two-story museum that was being renovated. After using a material hoist car to raise a drywall cart, he leaned on the rear door. The door opened, and the employee fell. The employee sustained blunt force traumatic injuries and was killed.

events.title: Postal Employee is killed after heat exposure
events.description: 1 worker death. Employer: U.S. Postal Service. Washington, DC. At 6:30 p.m. on July 22, 2020, an employee was delivering mail. Later, the employee was found unresponsive in the vehicle. The employee was killed and heat may have contributed to the employee's death.

events.title: Employee is killed when struck by falling hoe ram
events.description: 1 worker death. Employer: Miller And Long Company, Inc. Washington, DC. At 10:00 a.m. on June 30, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a concrete constructioncompany, was working at the demolition of a two-story commercial building. He was attaching a shackle to an excavator's hoe ram. The hoe ram became detached from the excavator and fell onto the employee. The employee sustained blunt force crushing injuries and was killed.

events.title: Employee with COVID-19 infection dies

events.title: Employee with COVID-19 infection dies

events.title: Two employees fall from building, Employee #1 is killed and…
events.description: 1 worker death. Employer: J.A.P. Home Improvement Inc. Washington, DC. At 2:00 p.m. on May 19, 2020, two employees were working to install floor decking on new multi-family home. At some point, Employee #1 and Employee #2 were struck by a sheet of plywood that was blown into them by a wind gust. Both employees were knocked off the decking and fell fifty feet. Employee #1 was killed and Employee #2 was hospitalized with unspecified injuries.

events.title: Employee driving concrete buggy is killed in crash
events.description: 1 worker death. Employer: Freedom Concrete, Llc. Washington, DC. At 10:30 a.m. on April 30, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a concrete construction company, was working at a multiemployer construction project, a three-story multifamily residential structure. He was driving a Georgia buggy (a motorized cart for hauling concrete and other materials) down a parking garage ramp when he lost control and crashed into a wood-framed plywood wall. Employee #1 sustained crushing injuries and was killed.

events.title: Employee dies of apparent drug overdose
events.description: 2 worker deaths. Employer: District Electrical Services. Washington, DC. At 1:30 p.m. on June 11, 2019, Employee #1, employed by an electrical services company, was working at a multiemployer construction project, a six-story multifamily residential structure. He was caulking wire penetrations when he lost consciousness. Emergency services were called, and upon their arrival Employee #1 was determined to have died. The apparent cause of death was a drugoverdose.

events.title: Employee on road crew is shot and killed
events.description: 1 worker death. Employer: Capitol Paving Of Dc. Washington, DC. At 4:15 p.m. on April 17, 2019, Employee #1, employed by a road paving company, was controlling traffic along a city street as his coworkers repaired the road. An unknown assailant shot Employee #1 in the chest. Employee #1 was killed by agunshot wound to his heart.

events.title: Employee is killed in fall from balcony

The employee leaned over too far, lost his balance and fell, striking clay pots and the ground below. Employee #1 sustained multiple fractures and was killed. killed.

events.title: Employee is killed when struck by falling tree limb
events.description: 1 worker death. Employer: Landsdown Tree Service, Llc. Washington, DC. At 11:15 a.m. on November 29, 2017, Employee #1 was working with a crew cutting tree limbs. A limb on the tree that the employee was standing under was cut, andfell on the employee, killing him.

events.title: Employee falls from scaffold and is killed
events.description: 1 worker death. Employer: Andiemac Waterproofing And Restoration, Llc. Washington, DC. At 2:00 p.m. on August 24, 2017, an employee was installing strips of bituminouswaterproofing materials along the exterior edge of the building's eleventh floorslab. The employee had been standing outside of the guardrails and jumped down to a platform made up of multi-point suspension scaffolding. The employee fell 80 feet from the scaffolding to the concrete slab and the employee was killed.

events.title: Employee falls from ladder and is killed
events.description: 1 worker death. Employer: Marcelo Gomes Construction Llc. Washington, DC. At 1:15 p.m. on May 24, 2017, an employee was nailing a second floor window intoplace. The employee was on the outside of the structure standing on a 32 feet extension ladder when reportedly he lost his balance and fell. The ladder was reportedly placed inside a 30 foot long construction dumpster among the trash and debris which possibly caused the ladder to slip. The employee was killed byimpact when hitting the ground.

events.title: Employee is buried at a construction site and is killed
events.description: 1 worker death. Employer: Bahia Construction Llc. Washington, DC. At 10:00 a.m. on February 28, 2017, an employee was checking footings at a construction site and a dirt wall collapsed, burying the employee.

events.title: Employee falls from scaffold and is killed
events.description: 1 worker death. Washington, DC. At approximately 4:30 a.m. on January 18, 2017, an employee was climbing the frames and cross bracing of a tubular welded frame scaffold in order to reach anelevated work platform. He fell 40 feet from the scaffold to a concrete slab below. The employee suffered severe trauma, including suspected multiple fractures, to all parts of the worker's body upon impact with the concrete slab and was killed.

events.title: Employee Dies from Overexposure to Toxic Atmosphere

events.title: Employee falls from roof and is killed
events.description: 1 worker death. Employer: Altamirano Contracting Services. Washington, DC. At approximately 3:00 p.m. on September 24, 2015, an employee, an owner, was installing tar paper on a roof. The employee fell 45 feet to the ground level. The employee suffered from multiple fractures and and was killed.

events.title: Employee is killed after falling from an elevated stage area…

The employee stepped off the open side of the stage and fell approximately 5 feet to the next lower level. The employee sustained fractured ribs when hitting the football playing surface and was killed.
